thread:
Taylor: quick sync: target GA checklist items and decision points for SLA/pricing/support. keeping it tight.
Ravi: high level yes. Need explicit latency tiers, uptime SLOs, escalation paths, and a pilot pricing construct.
Marta: For latency we should separate generation vs embedding profiles. Embeddings p99 is much lower and needs different guarantees.
Evan: Proposed SLA buckets:
- Platinum: embeddings p99 <= 50ms, gen small p99 <= 200ms, 99.95% uptime, 1h ack, 4h mitigation
- Platinum-Burst: same uptime, but dedicated burst pool guarantee for committed customers
- Standard: gen p99 <= 600ms, 99.5% uptime, 4h ack, 24h mitigation
- Community: best-effort, 99.0% uptime, forum support
Taylor: I like separating a burst guarantee variant. But legal wants to avoid promising hard latencies for large long-context models. Add "model-class exceptions" appendix.
LegalBot: Confirmed. We'll add a clause: "Latency targets apply to verified model profiles and typical-request-size distributions; exceptions documented per-model."
Ravi: Monitoring: per-tenant p50/p95/p99, error-rate, queue-depth, token throughput. Synthetic canaries every 5m per-region. Rollout gates defined on error_rate & quality checks.
Marta: On quality checks: add a "prompt-regression" monitor for high-volume customers using a baseline eval set. If quality drops, auto-route to fallback variant.
Evan: Runbook/ops: create an "GA incident play" that covers degraded model perf, cold-start regressions, KV-cache corruption and autoscale failures. Include roles: Pager, Triage, Customer comms, Escalation exec.
Taylor: Support matrix: Platinum -> 24/7 dedicated on-call + 15m phone escalation; Standard -> business hours + 1h email response; Community -> docs & slack. Also add onboarding SLA for Platinum pilots: three business-day setup for model onboarding and perf tuning.
FinOps: Pricing notes: Pilot discount for first 6 weeks, committed monthly tiers with reserved vGPU credits, and overage billed at burst rate. Need a clear example calc for customers.
Ravi: Rollout plan: internal dogfood -> 1% customer traffic for 48h -> 10% for 72h -> full with canary checks. Fallback policy: if error_rate > 0.4% for 15m OR p99 exceeds SLA by 30% for 10m, rollback traffic to previous variant.
Marta: Action items:
- Engineering (Evan): implement traffic-split + auto-rollback (due +4d)
- Monitoring (Ravi): dashboards + synthetic probes (due +3d)
- Docs (Taylor): customer SLA page + appendix + onboarding checklist (due +2d)
- Legal (LegalBot): finalized phrasing + exceptions appendix (due +5d)
- FinOps: pricing examples + pilot contract template (due +3d)
Taylor: Meeting ask: can infra confirm reserved-capacity headroom for 2 Platinum pilots next quarter? That blocks scheduling.
Evan: I'll ping infra. suspect yes but need explicit quota increase request.
FinOps: Also flag: we need to set margin guardrail for burst pricing, else pilots undercut revenue targets.
Ravi: One risk: unknown perf variance for long-context LLMs under high token rates. Recommend adding a "best-effort" note for contexts > 32k tokens and run an extended load test.
Taylor: Good call. Add load test to pre-GA checklist and a note in SLA appendix.
Marta: I'll draft the customer-facing SLA summary and the technical appendix mockups. Sharing in #product-docs by EOD.
Taylor: OK folks, if we close actions and infra confirms capacity, we can schedule a GA gating review next Thursday. Thanks. :thumbsup:
